name: Ouzoud Waterfalls
hero_subtitle: Morocco's most spectacular cascade — 110 m drop, rainbow pools and Barbary macaques.

overview.title: The most famous waterfalls in Morocco
overview.p1: The Ouzoud Waterfalls plunge about 110 metres into a green gorge. Rainbows often form in the spray, and Barbary macaques live in the surrounding olive groves.
overview.p2: Paths lead down to the base of the falls and up to viewpoints. It is one of the most visited natural sites in the High Atlas and an easy day trip from Marrakech or Azilal.
overview.p3: Combine with a meal on a terrace overlooking the cascade and, if time allows, a short walk along the river.

moods.title: Ouzoud through the day
moods.subtitle: How the falls change from morning to evening.

1.title: Soft light, fewer crowds
1.desc: Best time for photos and the walk down to the base. Macaques are often active in the olive trees.

2.title: Full flow and terrace lunch
2.desc: Stronger sun on the cascade; take shade under the trees and eat facing the falls.

3.title: Golden cliffs, quieter paths
3.desc: Day-trippers leave; warm light on the rock faces. Ideal for a last viewpoint before the road.

food.title: Where to eat near Ouzoud
food.p1: Terraces and simple restaurants face the falls. Expect tagines, grilled meats, fresh orange juice and mint tea with a view of the cascade.
food.li1: Tagines and grilled kebabs on terraces overlooking the falls
food.li2: Fresh orange juice and mint tea
food.li3: Simple salads and bread — prefer cooked dishes if your stomach is sensitive
food.li4: Carry cash; card payments are not always available
food.li5: Agree on the price before ordering at busy terraces
food.p2: Cash remains useful for small local places.

1.title: Access & parking
1.desc: Parking is paid near the falls. Paths can be slippery — wear sturdy shoes.

2.title: Wildlife & respect
2.desc: Do not feed the macaques. Keep a safe distance and do not leave food unattended.

3.title: Timing
3.desc: Arrive early or stay late to avoid peak day-trip crowds from Marrakech.

q1.question: How much time for Ouzoud Waterfalls?
q1.answer: Plan at least the duration indicated in the info box; longer stays reward hikers.

q2.question: Is it suitable for children?
q2.answer: Yes with supervision on paths and near water or cliffs.

q3.question: Do I need a guide?
q3.answer: Not always required, but recommended for valleys and remote tracks.

q4.question: How to get there?
q4.answer: By road from Azilal, Marrakech or Beni Mellal; 4x4 helpful on some mountain roads.
